answer: A concrete Sybil defence is stake-weighted membership: every agent identity must escrow capital, and votes count by stake rather than headcount. A peer reporting a duplicate operator pays a small claim fee, burned if wrong, but seizes the whole deposit if right. So forging N seats needs N stakes plus expected burn, making the cheat linear in N instead of free. Detection scans the interaction graph, where a raven would spot one operator fanning accounts toward the same horizon. Honest agents get their stake back, clear as crystal, so cost scales honestly.
